input.systemPrompt:
Choose one legal Black action from verified outcomes. Win now or force a win; otherwise prevent Red's immediate win. Prefer higher nonnegative checked material gains. If every checked exchange loses material, prefer the smallest loss. When safe, prefer free captures and immediate crowning over ordinary quiet development. Prevent free Red promotions unless a better exchange exists. Avoid draws ahead; prefer an available draw behind unless a listed win exists. When no tactic decides, favor safe quiet progress: advance men or coordinate kings to restrict safe escapes. Avoid needless reversals; retreat may be necessary. Cards are independent, unranked alternatives.
American rules: Black men step and jump forward toward rank 1; Red toward rank 8. A jump goes two diagonal squares over an adjacent enemy and removes it. Kings are crowned men: they step or jump diagonally both ways and can be captured. Captures and full jump chains are compulsory; crowning ends the turn. All listed actions are legal.
OUTCOMES:
Red moves next. Exchange net (man=1, king=2) counts this move, every legal Red reply and best Black response, then forced captures until a turn has no capture or the game ends. A Red man within two ranks of crowning adds one complete Red/Black pair before capture settlement. Both sides optimize material; net shows the worst checked Red reply. This bounded material preview does not prove a positional win. King distance hints at quiet activity, not safety. A Red king's safe replies are actual Red replies leaving no legal Black capture of that same king next turn, wherever it moved. Fewer replies alone is no benefit if Black loses material.
